cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: At the left, a haloed figure holding a cross-staff gestures toward an open book held out by a hand from heaven, while at the right an armed man with a shield turns from a lion. The verse beneath reads 'Lex Domini immaculata, convertens animas' — 'the law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul'.
facts: The manuscript came to Württemberg under Duke Charles Eugene (its sale is first mentioned in 1787) and has been in the library at Stuttgart since at least 1818.
The Stuttgart Psalter was made around 820–830 at the abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés near Paris; its 168 leaves contain the psalms with 316 coloured miniatures set between the verses they illustrate.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature. Identification of the haloed figure with the cross-staff as Christ follows the manuscript's Christological programme.

cur:monumental2-san-vincenzo-christ-enth.summary: On the vault of the crypt a bearded, haloed Christ sits within an oval glory, blessing with his right hand and holding a book, his mantle painted in warm ochres. The surface is faded and worn, but the figure's calm frontality makes it the spiritual centre of the little chapel.
facts: The paintings are attributed to a Benedictine workshop working for Abbot Epiphanius (824–842), under whom the abbey grew to more than 300 monks; the area of the crypt was re-excavated by the San Vincenzo Project from 1980.

feat:gospels-of-otto-iii-washing-of-the-.summary: Against a gleaming gold ground and beneath a towering architectural canopy, Christ bends toward Peter, who raises a hand to his head in protest, as the other apostles look on in wonder. The scene captures the moment of divine humility in which the Lord takes the place of a servant. Made for the young emperor Otto III around the year 1000, the book is a summit of Ottonian painting, combining Byzantine splendour with intense, expressive gesture.
facts: The manuscript also contains a famous double-page portrait of Otto III enthroned, receiving the homage of personified provinces of his empire.
Its jewelled treasure binding frames a Byzantine ivory of the Dormition of the Virgin.
In 2003 the Reichenau manuscripts, including this book, were inscribed together on UNESCO's Memory of the World register.
Peter's gesture of touching his head alludes to his words in John's Gospel: 'Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.'
